DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 25 s. 2022 20 April 2022 HON. WEBSTER D. LETARGO Municipal Mayor Gumaca, Quezon Dear Mayor Letargo: This has reference to your letter dated January 21 , 2022 requesting the Department's prompt and categorical pronouncement on the following issues: I. Can the Sangguniang Panlalawigan resolution revoke the resolution adopted by its Quasi-Judicial Body when the said resolution was already implemented? 2. Does the revocation by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Resolution No. 2021-01 of the Quasi-Judicial Body of Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Quezon has the effect of nullifying the Order of Preventive Suspension issued by the Govemor which was also sustained by the Regional Trial Court, Branch 172, Gumaca, Quezon in an Order dated January IO, 2022? Your aforesaid letter was forwarded to the Central Office by DILG-Region IV-A Director Ariel Iglesia in a letter dated January 24, 2022. Based on the documents forwarded to the Central Office, hereunder are the relevant factual antecedents: • With no budget approval in sight, you filed on November 16, 2021 before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP) of Quezon an Administrative Case for Oppression and Grave Abuse of Authority against the municipal vice-mayor and seven (7) sangguniang bayan members; • On December 20, 2021, after all the issues raised have been joined, the Vice- Governor, Hon. Samuel Nantes, and the remaining five (5) SP Members formed a Special Committee on Good Governance and Public Accountability which served as Quasi-Judicial Body of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Said Quasi- Judicial Body thereafter adopted Resolution No. 2021-01, recommending to Governor Danilo Suarez the preventive suspension of Vice-Mayor Erwin P. Caralian, SB Members Noel D. Dacillo, Marilou C. Mendoza, Femando B. Manalo, Prescilla Gina D. Magbuhos, Elenita B. Lumenario, Ramon Reynante Q. Castillo, PLB President, and Stephanie C. Marquez, PPKB President (hereinafter referred to as the "respondents"); Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

• Acting with dispatch, Governor Suarez issued Memorandum No. 328 preventively suspending the aforesaid officials and Memorandum No. 329, designating SB Member Rico J. Banal, the most senior among those not suspended SB members as the Acting Vice-Mayor; • The respondents immediately questioned their suspension by filing Civil Case No. 3494-G for Nullification of the Order of Preventive Suspension with Prayer for Temporary Restraining Order (T RO) and/or Preliminary Injunction before the RTC Gumaca, Quezon; • The respondents were able to obtain a 3-day TRO from the Vice Executive Judge, Maria Lourdes C. Gutierrez in the afternoon of December 23, 2022. Such TRO was made effective for a period of 72 hours or until the afternoon of December 26, 2021 ; • During the lifetime of the 72-hourTRO, particularly on December 25, 2021 , taking advantage of their majority number, the respondents held an online special session just to adopt a resolution nullifying everything that the Sangguniang Bayan composed of Acting Vice-Mayor Baäal and SB Members Ruvilon Juancho 'Mercurio and John Genmar Ylagan approved during special sessions of December 21 until 23, 2021. This includes the Annual Budget for FY 2021, Supplemental Budget No. I for FY 2021, and Annual Budget for FY 2022; • On December 29, 2022, respondents were able to obtain an extension of the TRO for additional seventeen (17) days or until January 15, 2022; • However, Acting Judge of RTC Branch 172, Hon. Michael E. Vito, issued an Order dated January IO, 2022 denying the respondents' prayer for Preliminary Injunction and accordingly, setting aside the order for the extension of the TRO dated December 29, 2021 ; • The Sangguniang Panlalawigan, during its session on January 14, 2022 adopted a resolution revoking/nullifying Kapasiyahan Blg. 2021-01 of the quasi-judicial body which recommended to Governor Suarez the preventive suspension of Vice-Mayor Caralian and 7 SB members of Gumaca, Quezon. They posit as the ground for revocation/nullification of the Kapasiyahan their claim that the suspended officials were not given the opportunity to appeal their suspension; • •On January 17, 2022 regular session, Vice-Mayor Caralian and the 7 other SB Members insisted on attending the session relying on the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Resolution revoking/nullifying Kapasiyahan Blg. 2021-01 but with utter disregard of the order of RTC Branch 172 reimposing their suspension; • On January 21 , 2022, the Office of the Mayor received a letter dated January 18, 2022 signed by Vice-Mayor Caralian and the 7 other SB Members With an excerpt of the transcription of the regular session the of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Quezon nullifying Kapasiyahan Blg. 2021-01 of the Quasi- Judicial Body of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Quezon. Page 2 of 5

We deem it proper to answer the two (2) issues raised in one (1) discussion since they are interrelated. Based on the recital of facts, a Special Committee on Good Governance and Public Accountability (referred to as the Quasi-JudiciaI Body of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan) composed of the remaining 5 SP Members adopted Resolution No. 2021-01 recommending to Governor Suarez the preventive suspension of Vice-Mayor Caralian and 7 other SB Members. Having the power to place respondents under preventive suspension, it follows that this so-called Quasi-Judicial Body of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan also has the power to revoke, provided however that such revocation shall be done in a proper case and under appropriate circumstances. In numerous legal opinions rendered by the Departmenti, we explained that the disciplining and investigating authority has the sole power and discretion to determine whether or not preventive suspension is warranted. Preventive suspension is thus said to be an incident to jurisdiction and/or tool for the disciplining authority, that is, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in this case, to make use of in the course of its administrative investigation. Thus, we also opined therein that the subsequent imposition of preventive suspension on the part of the governor or mayor upon the respondents is purely ministerial. In the event that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan decides to revoke its decision to place respondent under preventive suspension, it follows that there is no longer any basis for the governor or mayor to impose the preventive suspension upon the respondents since as we have already stated, the governor or mayor is only performing a ministerial function. At this juncture, it may be we well to emphasize that while the Sanggunian Panlalawigan has the power to revoke its decision to place respondent under preventive suspension, the same must be done in a proper case and under appropriate circumstances. As to what is an example of this proper case and appropriate circumstances, Section 63 of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 is instructive: "SECTION 63. Preventive Suspension. - (a) Preventive suspension may be imposed: xxx xxx (2) By the governor, if the respondent is an elective official of a component city or municipality; or xxx xxx (b) Preventive suspension may be imposed at any time after the issues are joined, when the evidence of guiit is strong, and given the gravity of the offense, there is great probability that the continuance in office of the respondent could influence the witnesses or pose a threat to the safety and integrity of the records and other evidence xxx" DILG Legal Opinion No. 44, series of 2004; DILG Legal Opinion No. 41, 2009. Page 3 of 5

Based on the foregoing, preventive suspension may be imposed only if all the following conditions are present: 1) Issues have already been joined; 2) When the evidence of guilt is strong; and 3) There is great probability that the continuance in office of the respondent could influence the witnesses or pose a threat to the safety and integrity of the records and other evidence. Therefore, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, as the Quasi-Judicial Body, may revoke the preventive suspension if any or all of the foregoing conditions are no longer present. Nevertheless, the Sanggunian Panlalawigan revoked or nullified Resolution No. 2021-01 on a claim that the suspended officials were not given the opportunity to appeal their suspension. which is not a condition for the revocation of the preventive suspension. Beside, this level noted that respondents were not denied the opportunity to appeal their preventive suspension. In the recital of facts, it was manifested that respondents immediately questioned their preventive suspension by filing Civil Case No. 3494-G for Nullification of the Order of Preventive Suspension with Prayer for Temporary Restraining Order (TRO) and/or Preliminary Injunction before the RTC Gumaca, Quezon. In fact, they were given a TRO and an extension, albeit set aside on January 10, 2022. It bears stressing that under Section 9 of A.O. 22 s. 2011, the preventive suspension of the respondents, as in this case, can be appealed to the Office of the President. Further, in Memorandum from the Executive Secretary dated December I, 2021 entitled "APPELLATE JURISDICTION FO THE OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT OVER SUSPENSION ORDERS AGAINST LOCAL ELECTIVE OFFICIALS" (OP Memorandum), the timely filing of the respondent of an appeal from decisions or orders of the sanggunian shall not automatically stay the execution of said san unian decisions or orders. Pertinent portion of the aforesaid OP Memorandum reads: "1. 2. 3. The timel filin before the OP of an a eal from decisions or orders issued b the San unians in administrative cases a ainst local elective officials shall not automaticall sta the execution thereof, pursuant to Section 9 of Administrative Order (AO) No. 22, s. 2011, in relation to Section 68 of the Local Government Code of 1991 The OP, however, has authority to order the stay of execution of the final decision or orders of suspension from office issued by the Sanggunians against local elective officials, pursuant to Section 9 of AO No. 22 and consistent with the Supreme Court ruling in Berces Sr. vs. Executive Secretary. The OP may likewise exercise appellate jurisdiction over orders of Sanggunians imposing preventive suspension against local elective officials, pursuant to Section I and 9 of AO No. 22, and the doctrine of exhaustion of administrative remedies. Moreover, this is in aid of the appellate jurisdiction of the OP over the decisions of such Sanggunians in administrative cases. Page 4 of 5

(Emphasis Supplied) A copy of the aforesaid OP Memorandum is hereto attached for your ready reference. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you.
